forest_10_001.speaker: narrator
forest_10_001.text: The inspector's spare boots stood beneath the map table while he read Pei's account. He asked when she found the fragment, who had handled it, and what she had told later applicants about the marker. Pei answered without her usual impatience. Lin watched the official record turn familiar stories into dated statements. The inspector did not ask whether Pei was a good keeper. He asked which useful facts her office had omitted when people sought the boundary.

forest_10_002.speaker: pei_yun
forest_10_002.text: I directed people to the higher stone for the winter road. Sometimes I let that answer stand when they asked about land. I knew the questions were different. I feared correcting one would endanger the other. The surviving road order shows the fear was mistaken. My original silence preceded finding that order; my later silence followed it. Please keep those periods distinct. I do not want eleven years of error made smaller by calling all of it confusion.

forest_10_003.speaker: narrator
forest_10_003.text: Rong and Long attended the public account because their applications had relied on the summary. The foreman arrived with the marking sheet. He asked whether the keeper's omission invalidated the hold. The inspector said no: an incomplete official answer justified examination, not automatic permission. He would determine the line from the available evidence and legal orders. Pei's responsibility for misleading guidance was a separate question. The foreman looked as though every separate question had become a wall between him and work.

forest_10_004.speaker: narrator
forest_10_004.text: The inspector examined the fragment under ordinary light. The witness mark matched the old survey's recorded position, and the surviving groove appeared consistent with its alignment description. Appearance would be checked against the base in the field. The fragment bore no modern land grant. Its value was location and orientation, not permission written in stone. Lin noticed Pei relax at the first match and tense at the warning. Even now, relief wanted to become more certainty than the object could supply.

forest_10_005.speaker: narrator
forest_10_005.text: The supposed confirmation copy lay beside the fragment. The inspector showed the missing notch in its seal and the added boundary phrase absent from the issued road order. The office had not issued that copy or authorized its conclusion. He could reject its authority now while the inquiry continued into who made and forwarded it. Rong gave the agent's address and his office's correspondence. Long gave the message that first mentioned the copy to his manager. Both had briefly hoped it was genuine.

forest_10_006.speaker: rong_sui
forest_10_006.text: My brother forwarded it after the agent said it would resolve the northern delay. He did not verify it with the land office. I did. The agent's covering note calls it a faithful office copy, which it is not. I will provide the original note and the receiving date. My employer will dislike seeing its convenient hope beside a false seal. That is a difficulty for my employer, not a reason to make this valley's records more accommodating.

forest_10_007.speaker: narrator
forest_10_007.text: The inspector asked the foreman whether he had acted on the purported confirmation. He said he had planned a renewed cut but had not sent the crew after Pei kept the hold. Wen watched his face closely. The foreman invited inspection of the tool roster and crew work dates. That invitation was useful. The inspector accepted it without congratulating him. A plan stopped before trees fell still deserved comparison with the actual work, especially when everyone had a reason to remember it favorably.

forest_10_008.speaker: narrator
forest_10_008.text: For the field survey, Pei remained a witness rather than sole guide. The inspector's assistant checked the old bridge datum, the previous team's measurements, and the surviving points independently. Lin accompanied the ordinary carrying and note turn. Wen came as a crew witness under paid travel terms, with his current knee clearance. Shi Lan joined for the passage and ground-safety questions. The inspector put on the spare boots because the first pair had already leaked crossing the village square.

forest_10_009.speaker: narrator
forest_10_009.text: At the lower bridge pier, the old cut mark still stood above the dark water. The inspector's assistant read it from the documented datum rather than adopting the commission's first sketch. His result agreed within the recorded measurement tolerance. Lin held the cord steady and felt absurdly pleased, as though her own honesty had received a mark. Then the assistant asked her to shift the support pin. The next reading required work, not emotional reward from the previous one.

forest_10_010.speaker: narrator
forest_10_010.text: The broken marker base emerged from the root tangle after loose snow was brushed aside under the inspector's direction. The team did not cut the living root that had pushed its setting. Pei watched from the stable path. Her fragment was brought beside the base without being forced into the broken face. Two visible fracture features corresponded. The assistant recorded the fit limits and orientation. The inspector could now identify the old marker more securely than by Pei's childhood memory alone.

forest_10_011.speaker: narrator
forest_10_011.text: Wen asked whether they would reassemble it. The inspector said a proper conservation and reset plan would be proposed after the line was certified; immediate reconstruction could obscure the condition they still needed to record. Wen nodded, disappointed in a way Lin understood. He wanted the broken thing visibly whole. Pei had wanted it privately safe. Both wishes reached past the object into histories the stone could not repair. The assistant continued measuring while they stood with those wishes.

forest_10_012.speaker: shi_lan
forest_10_012.text: The walking passage needs a visible current marker even while the old stone is conserved. Can your certification distinguish that practical route from the land line and the cart approach? We have spent enough years pointing at the nearest upright thing and hoping the listener asks the same question we meant to answer. The new boards should name all three. I will have the gathering households inspect the route descriptions before the office orders a handsome set nobody uses correctly.

forest_10_013.speaker: narrator
forest_10_013.text: The inspector agreed. They continued to the second fixed point, where the old notice-frame holes survived in the rock. The assistant measured from both directions, using the stable pier and the documented turn. The two checks converged within the accepted tolerance. The newer road stone lay outside the old land segment, as the first inquiry suggested. The surveyed winter passage crossed below it and widened at the shallow bank the Hart had described. Memory, record, and current use were finally meeting on the same slope.

forest_10_014.speaker: narrator
forest_10_014.text: Pei stood near the resting tree while the others recorded the turn. Lin joined her after setting down the empty rod case. The keeper said her father had carved the witness mark badly because he was cold. Lin said she remembered the chicken story. Pei smiled and then cried without covering her face. The tears embarrassed neither of them as much as Lin expected. A witness could grieve while the measurement remained a measurement. The assistant called for the case, and Lin returned to work.

forest_10_015.speaker: pei_yun
forest_10_015.text: I kept the fragment as if taking care of my father's mark meant taking care of his work. His work was to make the line answerable after he was gone. I made part of it answerable only to me. You do not need to say anything kind about that. Stay beside me until I finish this sentence, if you can. Then go carry the rods. He would have liked that better than another speech from his daughter.

forest_10_016.speaker: narrator
forest_10_016.text: On the upper return, the foreman identified every fresh stump from the disputed cut. The surveyed old line placed part of the cutting outside the approved commercial stand. The exact timber disposition and liability required the land office's formal decision and affected owners' statements. The inspector marked the location findings for that decision. He did not grant the foreman a new right because confusion had been widespread. He also recorded Pei's misleading guidance and the buyer clerk's report as possible contributing facts.

forest_10_017.speaker: narrator
forest_10_017.text: The foreman said he had followed the visible marker everyone used. Pei answered that she had helped make that use misleading. The inspector asked each to keep the statements separate. Wen looked from one to the other, no longer able to imagine a single villain whose removal would leave the family untroubled. The trees were cut. Someone would have to account for the loss, the labor, the mistaken instructions, and the people who had expected wages from all of it.

forest_10_018.speaker: narrator
forest_10_018.text: They stopped at the western shelter for lunch. The inspector's leaking boots stood near the stove, carefully far enough away not to scorch. Wen offered him a bean cake. The inspector bit the edge and looked startled. Lin said the recipe had improved since the first batch. The official replied that he admired a cake with enough structural integrity to support a survey marker. Pei laughed, then wiped her eyes with the same cloth. The day permitted both acts.

forest_10_019.speaker: narrator
forest_10_019.text: On the way down, the Hart pair crossed the quiet bank during its posted interval. The inspector watched from the widened waiting place with the gathering households. The adult looked toward Lin and did not speak. It did not need to. The route itself supplied the relevant observation: people and the two large bodies passed without competing for the narrow corner. The official added the current crossing to his field note, leaving the wildlife account to its own qualified office.

forest_10_020.speaker: narrator
forest_10_020.text: At the gate, the gathering woman inspected the proposed three-name route board. She said the path called lower winter passage in the office was called auntie's bend by half the village. Pei added the common name beneath the formal one. The inspector looked amused until the woman asked whether his next report would use words her grandson could follow. He promised a public route copy beside the legal certification. She said promises were easier than spelling and remained to check the draft.

forest_10_021.speaker: narrator
forest_10_021.text: The team returned with a measured line, an identified marker fragment, and several claims still requiring judgment. Lin's hands were numb from the cord and her head tired from everyone's disappointment. Pei walked beside her without giving instructions. At the office door, the keeper let the inspector enter first. It was a small change in an old habit. Inside, the dry table waited for the stone, which had finally become public evidence instead of a private answer no one knew to request.

forest_10_022.speaker: narrator
forest_10_022.text: The old line divided the approved commercial coppice from three household wood lots, while the winter passage crossed under separately recorded access terms. The rebuilt cart approach served a different route and had not transferred those lots to commercial use. The inspector prepared a preliminary location certification, leaving current ownership claims and compensation for the formal hearing. Two households were present. The third's current representative lived beyond the winter ridge and would need proper notice rather than a neighbor volunteering an answer.

forest_10_023.speaker: narrator
forest_10_023.text: One present household had already lost timber to the disputed cut. Its owner brought a child-sized walking stick made from an older branch of the same stand. He did not wave it as evidence; he leaned on it while describing which trees the family expected to use over the next winters. The cut had taken future household fuel and useful stems, not merely a seasonal number of charcoal bags. The foreman listened with the marking sheet folded small between his hands.

forest_10_024.speaker: narrator
forest_10_024.text: The second household cared most about the passage. Its elder could no longer manage the longer high bend every day. She accepted the current protected crossing intervals but wanted the final route agreement to survive after the Hart pair moved on. The inspector recorded the request beside the old access terms. Lin understood then why the animal's successful crossing could not settle every human claim. A route useful to two frightened bodies might also be the only tolerable path for a woman who walked slowly.

forest_10_025.speaker: pei_yun
forest_10_025.text: I guided both your families by the higher stone when you asked where the road was. I did not explain the land line consistently. That helped the commercial application look simpler than it was. I have brought my full statement to the inspector. You may ask it to be read into the hearing. I will not ask you to forgive me before it is. I can still help locate the older papers, if you want my help under another person's check.

forest_10_026.speaker: narrator
forest_10_026.text: The owner with the walking stick asked why he should trust her now. Pei said he did not have to rely on her alone. The measured certification, road order, and fragment record were available through the inspector. She would supply what she knew for comparison. The answer pleased nobody enough to end the matter. It did let the owner request a particular old household allocation page instead of spending the entire afternoon deciding whether Pei deserved to sit behind her desk.

forest_10_027.speaker: narrator
forest_10_027.text: The inspector certified the location findings for the current hold and hearing preparation. The disputed logs would remain separated; new cutting there stayed unauthorized. A later disposition might use some logs to compensate affected households in timber or fuel, subject to ownership and condition. The seasonal approved output estimate still excluded them. Long asked whether that exclusion would remain even if one household chose to sell. The inspector said a lawful later sale could be assessed then, not anticipated as current stock now.

forest_10_028.speaker: narrator
forest_10_028.text: Rong asked about his advance remedy's removal. The inspector confirmed the revised business agreement did not gain a northern right from the field findings. Rong nodded, looking neither delighted nor surprised. The foreman asked whether Pei's misleading guidance reduced his liability. The formal hearing would consider it along with the buyer's false report and his own cutting instruction. He would have a chance to submit his account. He looked tired of chances that did not arrive carrying immediate absolution.

forest_10_029.speaker: narrator
forest_10_029.text: After the public session, Pei handed the office's survey drawer key to the temporary records deputy appointed by the council. She retained ordinary keeper duties pending review, but boundary certifications and applications now required the independent officer's check. The deputy inventoried the drawer with her present. Lin watched the stone fragment's former hiding place become an ordinary empty compartment. Pei looked at it once, then returned to sorting the loose papers that had fallen behind the cabinet.

forest_10_030.speaker: narrator
forest_10_030.text: Among the loose papers lay a child's drawing of the old bridge. Pei recognized it as her nephew's. She asked to keep it after the deputy verified it contained no official record. The little request hurt Lin more than the key handover had. It made the cabinet seem like a life as well as an office, a place where useful memory and private tenderness had accumulated until Pei could no longer tell which things she had a duty to show.

forest_10_031.speaker: narrator
forest_10_031.text: Wen met Lin outside and asked whether the field findings changed his crew's work. Licensed cutting and kiln handling could continue under the current schedule. The disputed stand remained closed. He said his foreman had hoped the keeper's fault would make the crew's fault disappear. Lin said she had hoped exposing the fragment would make her own trust simple again. Wen looked at her and said perhaps everyone had been trying to purchase something impossible from the same broken stone.

forest_10_032.speaker: wen_cai
forest_10_032.text: I am angry with Pei too. I still remember her giving me a place to file the foreman's threat when my uncle would not speak. That happened. Her hiding the fragment happened. I do not know how to put them together without making one smaller. My sister says I like single feelings because my uncle taught me. I have been improving at mixed ones. Today I would like a holiday from the improvement.

forest_10_033.speaker: narrator
forest_10_033.text: They took their holiday at the kitchen table, where the cook served cabbage noodles and forbade discussion of markers until bowls were empty. Wen lasted four bites before mentioning stone indirectly as a complaint about the noodle's firmness. The cook hit his sleeve lightly with a clean towel. Lin laughed hard enough to spill broth. Pei entered at that moment, saw the wet table, and fetched the wiping cloth without asking what had caused the laughter.

forest_10_034.speaker: narrator
forest_10_034.text: The keeper sat at the table's end. Nobody moved away. Nobody invited her to make a speech. Shi Lan asked whether she had eaten, and Pei answered with a look that made Wen visibly struggle not to laugh again. She accepted a bowl. The ordinary meal did not reverse the public statement or restore the drawer key. It gave a person who had failed badly somewhere to sit while the next day arrived. Lin found she could allow that without pretending not to be angry.

forest_10_035.speaker: narrator
forest_10_035.text: That evening, the household with the walking stick asked the council for replacement winter fuel pending the timber-loss hearing. The emergency allocation could provide a limited bridge portion from existing council stock, with the claim preserved for later settlement. The owner accepted after inspecting the wood. He wanted longer stems for next year's repairs too; those were not in the emergency pile. The council recorded the separate request. The forest's cut trees had produced several kinds of absence.

forest_10_036.speaker: narrator
forest_10_036.text: Long received the supplier's paid stock inspection. The smaller remaining quantity was sound and not already pledged elsewhere, but the receiving date depended on a limited carriage slot. Rong wanted to divide the commercial reservation between their offices. Long wanted the whole quantity for valley kitchens, arguing town households had more alternatives. Rong answered that his remaining town customers were precisely those who lacked alternatives. Their improved information had narrowed the dispute until its real discomfort stood in the open.

forest_10_037.speaker: long_qian
forest_10_037.text: I cannot tell a kitchen to cook every other day while we arrange a fairer phrase. Your town customers can ask family for another stove in an emergency. Some can. Not all. I know you will say that, and you will be right. I am still responsible for meals here. If I reserve the whole outside lot, my clients are safer and yours are less safe. That is the choice I am tempted to make. I will not call it a neutral efficiency.

forest_10_038.speaker: narrator
forest_10_038.text: Rong said his office could reserve independently, but doing so would start a price contest neither needed. He proposed splitting the verified limited lot provisionally while both identified the highest immediate needs. The reservation would be paid by their business funds, not charged to the council's household stock. Long accepted a short discussion interval before the carriage slot expired. Lin watched them return to their desks. Cooperation had survived only because each admitted what he might do without it.

forest_10_039.speaker: narrator
forest_10_039.text: At the clinic, the boy was cleared for discharge under an ordinary home-care plan when the household could provide warmth, clean dressings, and the advised reduced movement. His grandmother and mother arranged those conditions with the assistant. He would return for checks; lasting damage to the toes remained uncertain. Wen delivered the larger boot's fitting appointment, which would wait until swelling settled. The boy asked whether that meant he had to remain barefoot forever. The assistant said forever was not today's instruction.

forest_10_040.speaker: narrator
forest_10_040.text: Lin helped carry the family's bags for the homeward cart, leaving the medical tasks to those assigned. The boy sat wrapped beside his grandmother and waved at the paper dog, whose guardian had reclaimed it after the visit. The niece waved the dog back. The cart moved by the safe lower route. In the shelter, the closed shortcut board stayed where it belonged. A child going home did not make the ditch repaired. It did make the clinic room ready for the next person needing warmth.

forest_10_041.speaker: narrator
forest_10_041.text: After the cart left, Lin sat alone for a short while beside the empty clinic bench. She had not saved the boy's foot by any spectacular skill. She had run a message, washed cloths, carried bags, and listened badly before listening better. The work felt both insufficient and real. When Wen found her, he did not ask which feeling had won. He asked whether she wanted to walk to his sister's house, where someone was apparently making bean cakes with a softer edge.

forest_10_042.speaker: narrator
forest_10_042.text: They went. The cakes were indeed softer, which the uncle attributed to a method he had recommended and the sister attributed to ignoring him until the dough rested. The intended husband refused to adjudicate. Lin ate two and considered the refusal wise. Outside, the winter sky had begun clearing over the newly measured line. Pei's fragment lay secured in the office, available to more than one pair of eyes. The route boards would need painting. The people eating cakes would need tomorrow's work.

forest_10_043.speaker: narrator
forest_10_043.text: The outside lot contained twelve dry bags, smaller than the earlier quotation because other customers had bought the rest during the road closure. Rong and Long agreed to reserve six each, with confirmed receiving conditions and a carriage date. The imported bags stayed outside the local seasonal estimate. Their cost came from the buyers' business accounts, including the paid inspection. The reservation could ease a later shortage. It did not justify promising the northern extensions again.

forest_10_044.speaker: narrator
forest_10_044.text: Rong signed his half and asked Long whether he still hated sharing the lot. Long said yes. Rong said he did too. They both laughed, surprised by the ease of naming an unpleasant fact after the decision was made. Lin carried the paired reservation to the courier desk. She thought the laugh sounded less like friendship than relief from a price contest they had avoided. That was sufficient. The cart would still have to bring actual fuel over an actual road.

forest_10_045.speaker: narrator
forest_10_045.text: The three route boards were painted the next day. Each named the cart approach, the household passage, and the protected crossing turn distinctly, with familiar village names beneath the formal ones. Pei checked spelling under the deputy's review and accepted a correction from the gathering woman without snapping. The boy's grandmother came to see which board would stand near the safe turn. She said the letters needed to be larger. The painter enlarged them before the paint dried.

forest_10_046.speaker: narrator
forest_10_046.text: Wen helped place the first board with the qualified path worker. Lin carried the smaller pins and held the level. The old road stone remained upright above them, now labeled for the cart approach instead of asked to answer every question. The fragment and base would be conserved under the approved later plan. Pei stood nearby, watching the new board rather than touching the old stone. The road kept its use while the land line acquired its own visible words.

forest_10_047.speaker: narrator
forest_10_047.text: At the resting tree, the household elder inspected the passage board from her usual approach. The lower line of writing was hidden by a branch. Shi Lan had the board shifted to a readable position clear of the crossing. The elder nodded. Lin liked the bluntness of the test: a board made for walkers had failed if one walker could not see it. The painter grumbled about moving his hole, then dug a better one. Useful criticism had a shovel attached.

forest_10_048.speaker: narrator
forest_10_048.text: The adult Hart watched the placement from beyond the shallow bank. It did not approach the paint or the people. The youngster stood beside it, still carrying the injured leg carefully. Shi Lan gave them room and finished the board before the protected interval began. Lin spoke only to say the crossing would remain clear. The Hart inclined its head once. The gesture was small enough that the watch recorded it as movement rather than invent a pledge from it.

forest_10_049.speaker: narrator
forest_10_049.text: At the office, the formal hearing schedule was set for the sixteenth commission week, allowing notice to the absent household representative and time for the timber, custody, and forged-copy inquiries. The current location certification and cutting hold applied meanwhile. Compensation claims could receive limited interim relief without waiting for final judgment. Lin read the dates and felt the season stretch. Some stories moved quickly because a body was in danger. Others moved slowly because a decision had to reach people not standing at the desk.

forest_10_050.speaker: narrator
forest_10_050.text: The foreman submitted a preliminary loss claim against the buyer's misleading report and Pei's office guidance. Rong submitted his own corrected letters and offered credit record. Pei gave the full custody statement. The affected households claimed the timber loss and access disruption. Their accounts contradicted one another in places and overlapped in others. The inspector's office would sort them before the hearing. Lin was assigned only to copy the public location notice, which was plenty of responsibility for one afternoon.

forest_10_051.speaker: narrator
forest_10_051.text: The town forwarding agent replied about the purported confirmation. He said a supplier representative had brought it as a useful old-office copy and asked him to send it to buyers interested in northern timber. He provided the receiving date and the representative's trade address. The name on the address belonged to the winter contractor whose route quotation had first ignored the closure. Rong looked at the two files side by side. Convenience was beginning to have a recurring source.

forest_10_052.speaker: narrator
forest_10_052.text: The contractor denied making the copy. He said he had received it from a traveling clerk and believed the seal. The land office requested the original covering message, the clerk's identification if known, and the places where the contractor had used the page commercially. Until verification, no office would accept the copy as authority. The contractor could still offer ordinary lawful carriage under independently checked terms. Rong's brother wanted him excluded entirely. Rong said evidence should decide the forgery claim, not humiliation.

forest_10_053.speaker: rong_sui
forest_10_053.text: If we ban a man because he embarrassed my office, I will have supplied him with a grievance stronger than the page he forwarded. If he knowingly altered it, the land inquiry must establish that and act. If he passed a false copy carelessly, that still matters. I want his actual documents. My brother wants a conclusion before supper. One of those requests can be answered by the next messenger, and it is not the second.

forest_10_054.speaker: narrator
forest_10_054.text: Long was less patient. The contractor had nearly induced an early reservation and now appeared in the false boundary chain. He said the grain house would not use him while the inquiry continued. That was a commercial decision Long could make under his own accounts. Rong did not argue. Cooperation did not require both offices to trust the same carrier. Lin wondered whether her own new suspicion of Pei was similar: a limit she could choose without pretending it was a court judgment.

forest_10_055.speaker: narrator
forest_10_055.text: She spoke to Pei after the office closed. She said she wanted another person's check on any new boundary copy she assisted. Pei said the deputy's review already provided that, and Lin could request the specific comparison. The keeper looked hurt, then composed. She asked whether Lin still wanted to hear old forest stories when they were clearly offered as stories. Lin said yes. She had not lost the pleasure of Pei's voice. She had lost the habit of letting pleasure certify its facts.

forest_10_056.speaker: pei_yun
forest_10_056.text: Then I will tell you one after dinner that contains no boundary at all. A goose may appear. The tax assistant may be embarrassed. Nobody will acquire land through the ending. I cannot promise perfect wisdom from the storyteller. I can promise to say when I do not remember whether the goose was white or grey. My father used to change that detail depending on how muddy the assistant looked in his imagination.

forest_10_057.speaker: narrator
forest_10_057.text: The story contained two geese by the time the niece joined it, and a third when Wen arrived. Pei protested the additions until the child asked whether the official version had been certified. The keeper laughed so unexpectedly that everyone stopped teasing for a moment. Lin stayed through the whole story. Afterwards, she returned the public copy she had checked to the deputy's file. A friendship could reopen at the table while its working safeguards remained in the office.

forest_10_058.speaker: narrator
forest_10_058.text: During the week's last field turn, Shi Lan and the deputy reviewed the hollow's drainage proposal. The winter passage could remain usable through the protected intervals, but the low pools would continue freezing over hazards until a careful drainage repair was designed. The design needed to protect the refuge's water and roots while clearing the unsafe gathering approach. Excavating the whole hollow would solve one access problem by making several new ones. The proposal would go to a qualified water worker, not to Lin's shovel enthusiasm.

forest_10_059.speaker: narrator
forest_10_059.text: Lin accepted the limit with less resentment than she expected. Her shovel work had taught her enough to see what she did not know, including how hidden roots and water changed a tidy surface. She assisted the measurements and carried the sample jars the deputy requested. Wen walked beside her with the ordinary tools. They were not heroic equipment. The late afternoon light made them gleam anyway, which amused her more than it should have.

forest_10_060.speaker: wen_cai
forest_10_060.text: You are smiling at a jar. I would like the record to show that the forest has finally damaged your standards of entertainment. We can stop at the shelter before returning. The senior worker has promised tea from his professionally dressed kettle. If you admire that too openly, he will become impossible. He already says the knitted sleeve has improved morale more than three meetings. I suspect he is right, which makes the claim worse.

forest_10_061.speaker: narrator
forest_10_061.text: At the shelter, the tea was hot and the kettle looked splendidly foolish. The watch had seen the Hart pair pass without an encounter that day. The boy's grandmother had completed her carried wood turn. The charcoal kiln schedule continued within the approved plan, and the imported twelve bags had a confirmed loading appointment. Lin drank and let the facts be ordinary good news. The forest would invent enough trouble later without her rehearsing it while the tea was still warm.

forest_10_062.speaker: narrator
forest_10_062.text: The next morning, the carriage station sent notice of a mixed commercial convoy arriving in the eighth commission week. It would bring the buyers' reserved charcoal in separately covered loads and ordinary grain for the lower stores, each under its own receiving agreement. The road limit and staggered crossing schedule were included. Long read the notice twice. Rong checked the driver list. Shi Lan asked which watch turn would keep gatherers clear of the unloading lane without closing their whole morning.

forest_10_063.speaker: narrator
forest_10_063.text: They arranged the lane and funded the ordinary receiving work from the respective buyers' carriage accounts. Lin would assist the public route watch, not certify commercial stock. Wen had a paid unloading turn under the keeper's handling schedule. The plan looked modest enough to succeed. Pei filed the final field notes and gave the deputy the drawer key before leaving. Outside, the reopened road ran pale between dark trees. Somewhere beyond the ridge, the convoy was loading weight the valley had been waiting to believe in.

forest_10_064.speaker: narrator
forest_10_064.text: Before the convoy week, Long visited the boy's household to ask whether the borrowed handcart had met the revised carrier demand. He brought the clerk responsible for its schedule, ready to hear the practical answer. The grandmother said the cart worked and the first loading point still grew icy. The clerk noted the need for grit there. The boy showed Long his new larger boot, not yet worn outside. Long admired it with the solemnity he usually gave scales.

forest_10_065.speaker: narrator
forest_10_065.text: The boot had room for the healing foot and would be adjusted after swelling changed. The boy wanted to wear it immediately. His grandmother pointed to the home-care instructions. He sighed with the magnificence of a child suffering adulthood's unreasonable patience. Long asked whether the other boot matched. It did, though the cobbler had used different leather at the toe. The boy said he preferred the odd patch because it made the pair look adventurous. His grandmother said adventure had already cost enough this winter.

forest_10_066.speaker: narrator
forest_10_066.text: Lin arrived later with the family's approved carrier bundle and found the boy drawing the safe route. His first map made the Hart larger than the bridge and the clinic larger than the village. She asked him where the ditch was. He drew it carefully, then put a warning mark beside it. The grandmother said they would show the map at the next access review if he wished. He did. Lin liked that the boy could contribute a fact without having to turn his accident into a performance.

forest_10_067.speaker: narrator
forest_10_067.text: At the clinic's next check, the boy's ankle was improving and the cold-injured skin was healing unevenly, with no new immediate complication. Reduced movement and dressing care continued. The assistant would not promise the toes would feel normal by the marriage meal. The boy asked whether sitting at the feast counted as attending. Wen said it counted best if someone brought him the favorite dish first. The boy accepted that standard and asked who would enforce it. Wen nominated the niece, creating a formidable institution.

forest_10_068.speaker: narrator
forest_10_068.text: Pei helped the household representative beyond the ridge receive proper notice through the courier station. The notice included the measured location findings, the hearing date, and the means to submit a statement without an unsafe winter journey. A reply would take time. The temporary deputy checked the address against the household's current recorded contact. Pei had remembered an older address. She accepted the correction quietly. Lin saw how review could catch an ordinary mistake before it grew into another secret.

forest_10_069.speaker: narrator
forest_10_069.text: Rong went to the kiln to verify the next lawful delivery against the agreed schedule. The foreman made his second four-copper installment when that income came in, leaving thirty-two copper of the revised forty-copper balance. No new crew contribution was requested. The injured worker's long-term accident claim remained at its own hearing stage, with the employer's proposed reassignment subject to medical clearance. Rong kept the debt receipt and the injury file separate, as promised. Lin was grateful he did not make her admire the separation aloud.

forest_10_070.speaker: narrator
forest_10_070.text: The worker whose shoulder had been strained returned to a limited light shift after review. He had slept through the previous night and no longer tried to prove his usefulness with a heavier bundle. At the sack bench, he taught Lin a better finishing knot. Wen said her stitched sack might now receive respectable visitors. The worker said it could receive twelve kilograms and no flattery. Lin tied the knot again until it held flat. Ordinary competence had become pleasantly stubborn.

forest_10_071.speaker: narrator
forest_10_071.text: Shi Lan took the niece to the resting tree during a clear safe interval when the watch confirmed the Hart pair was farther uphill. The girl wanted to see the place her paper animal lived. The warden showed her the crossing without approaching the animals or collecting antler dust. She asked why the tree had no name on the board. Shi Lan said some things could remain trees. The girl named it Potato anyway and promised not to require the office to record it.

forest_10_072.speaker: narrator
forest_10_072.text: On the way home, the niece asked whether Pei had been bad when she hid the stone. Shi Lan stopped walking before answering. She said Pei had done a bad thing and was answering for it. The girl asked whether she could still tell stories. Shi Lan said yes, and other people would check the official work. The child considered this and asked whether her own stolen jam confession should receive similar treatment. The warden said the jam inquiry would be conducted at supper.

forest_10_073.speaker: narrator
forest_10_073.text: The confession turned out to concern a spoonful from the cook's pot, taken before permission. The cook assigned the child a small supervised washing task and reclaimed the jar. Wen said the penalty was merciful. The cook said she could extend it to commentators. He went silent. Pei arrived midway through the washing and pretended not to understand why the child looked so embarrassed. Lin watched the kindness and the enforced consequence share the same warm room without becoming a lesson anyone had to announce.

forest_10_074.speaker: narrator
forest_10_074.text: That night the convoy runner reached the valley with the final departure confirmation. The commercial loads had been weighed and covered, the drivers accepted the crossing schedule, and the road office had supplied the current limit. Weather remained cold but within the ordinary transport plan. The valley receiving crews would be ready at the posted time. Long slept badly anyway. Rong wrote one last letter to his brother, then stopped before adding another paragraph of reassurance that contained no new fact.

forest_10_075.speaker: narrator
forest_10_075.text: Before dawn, Lin heard the senior worker singing Pei's romantic verse while filling his dressed kettle. He claimed the tune helped keep his hands warm. Wen said the words suggested another explanation. Shi Lan told them both to stop before the niece learned a fourth verse the office would regret. Lin smiled into her ordinary breakfast. The measured boundary had changed the ground people could claim, but the day ahead depended on simpler things: sound wheels, clear roads, and drivers who arrived with the weight they had promised.
